question.text: A ball rolls off the top of a stairway with horizontal velocity <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>u</mi></math>. The steps are <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>1</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math> high and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>1</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math> wide. The minimum velocity <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>u</mi></math> with which that ball just hits the step <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>5</mn></math> of the stairway will be <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msqrt><mi>x</mi></msqrt><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>, where <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo></math>_______ [use <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>g</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math>].

solution.text:
The ball needs to just cross 4 steps to just hit 5th step

Therefore, horizontal range

R=4×0.1 m= 0.4 m

The formula to calculate the horizontal range is given by

R=ut   ...1

Similarly, the vertical height covered by the ball is given by

h=12gt2   ...2

From equations (1) and (2), it follows that

4×0.1=12gt2⇒0.4=12 g0.4u2⇒u2=2⇒u=2 m s-1

Therefore, x=2.
